Accessibility

A class site should work for the whole class. Here is what we do on purpose, and how to tell us when it does not.

Everything works from the keyboard

Tab through the site and you can reach every link, button, menu, and form field. There is a skip-to-content link at the top of every page. Nothing requires a mouse.

You can always see where you are

Focused elements get a clear purple outline. We never hide it. Buttons and tap targets are at least 44 pixels tall so they are easy to hit on a phone.

Motion respects your settings

If your device has Reduce Motion turned on, the countdown flip, the scroll-in reveals, and the confetti all switch off. Nothing autoplays with sound.

Contrast in both themes

Text meets WCAG AA contrast against its background in light and dark mode. Color is never the only way information is shown: status labels and date labels always include words.

Alt text and structure

Photos on the photos page use their captions as alt text, which is why the submission form asks you to describe what is in the photo. Decorative art is hidden from screen readers. Pages use real headings, lists, and landmarks so they read in order.

Standards

We build to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA and test with a keyboard, a screen reader, browser zoom at 200%, and both color themes before pages go live. We are students, not an audit firm, so we will miss things. When we do, we fix them fast and say so.

Known limits right now: uploaded photos depend on the caption the submitter wrote, and content we link to on outside sites is theirs, not ours.

Hit a wall?

Tell us the page, what you were trying to do, and what happened, plus which browser or assistive tech you use if you know. Accessibility reports are handled alongside corrections, ahead of everything else.
